title: Principle Splitters
blurb: Two near-identical situations, one flipped fact — name the principle each one illustrates.

pairs.dimension: whether the harm is biased outcomes or blocked access

a.text: A hiring model shortlists far fewer candidates from one demographic group despite equal qualifications.
a.why: Unequal outcomes across groups is fairness — fixed with balanced training data and fairness assessments.

b.text: The same hiring portal's AI screening works only by voice, so deaf candidates cannot complete it at all.
b.why: Nobody is scored unfairly — some users are locked out. Multiple interaction methods and accessibility are inclusiveness.

pairs.dimension: whether the gap traces to underrepresented training data or to a single required interaction method

a.text: A retailer's shoplifting-detection camera system, trained mostly on images of one demographic group, flags people from other groups at a much higher rate.
a.why: An accuracy gap traceable to underrepresented training data across demographic groups is fairness — representative, balanced training data is the fix.

b.text: The same retailer's self-checkout assistant accepts only spoken commands, so customers who cannot speak or hear clearly cannot use it at all.
b.why: No group is scored worse here — an entire set of users is shut out by relying on one interaction method. That access gap is inclusiveness, not a scoring problem.

pairs.dimension: disclosing how the system works vs owning its outcomes

a.text: The bank publishes a model card explaining the credit model's capabilities and known limitations.
a.why: Communicating capabilities AND limitations — model cards, transparency notes — is transparency.

b.text: The bank keeps audit logs of every AI credit decision and names the officer who signs off on overrides.
b.why: Human oversight, governance and a reviewable record of who is answerable is accountability.

pairs.dimension: explaining one already-made decision vs assigning who owns it if it goes wrong

a.text: When a patient's insurance claim is denied by a triage model, the care team can point to the specific factors that drove that particular denial.
a.why: Explaining the specific reasons behind one already-made decision, to the person it affected, is transparency.

b.text: The hospital defines who is responsible for reviewing a denial and escalating it if the triage model's decision turns out to be wrong.
b.why: Assigning ownership and an escalation path for when things go wrong is accountability — who answers for the outcome, not what gets disclosed.

pairs.dimension: protecting the data vs disclosing the behavior

a.text: The support bot is configured so customer PII never appears in responses or logs.
a.why: PII governance, data protection and access control map to privacy & security.

b.text: The support bot opens every session stating it is an AI and listing what it can and cannot help with.
b.why: Disclosing what the system is and its limits is transparency — a different obligation from protecting data.

pairs.dimension: communicating limitations vs behaving safely under adverse input

a.text: Release notes state the summarizer performs poorly on legal documents so users can judge when to trust it.
a.why: Stating limitations up front is transparency, even though it feels safety-adjacent.

b.text: The summarizer is stress-tested with adversarial prompts and refuses to produce harmful content under them.
b.why: Consistent, tested, safe behavior under risky prompts — content filters and model evaluation — is reliability & safety.

pairs.dimension: whether the risk is harmful output behavior or exposure of personal data

a.text: A content-moderation service must resist adversarial prompts that try to make it generate violent instructions.
a.why: Resisting adversarial prompts to keep output from turning harmful is tested, consistent system behavior — reliability & safety.

b.text: The same service must keep customer phone numbers typed into chat messages from ever appearing in stored logs.
b.why: Keeping personal data out of storage and logs is data protection — a different concern from how the model behaves under attack.

pairs.dimension: whether the gap is about who can use the system or what users are told about it

a.text: A financial-advice chatbot adds screen-reader-compatible output and keyboard-only navigation so people with visual or motor impairments can complete a session end to end.
a.why: Removing barriers so people with different abilities can use the product at all is inclusiveness.

b.text: The same chatbot opens every session stating it is an automated assistant and listing the topics it is not qualified to advise on.
b.why: Disclosing that the system is AI and stating its limits is a different obligation from making the interface usable to everyone.
